Task: Develop a complete lesson plan for teaching probability to high-school students.

Complete Lesson Plan: Introduction to Probability  
Target Audience: High-school students (Grades 9-10) in a general or honors mathematics course  
Total Class Time: Two 55-minute periods (can be condensed or expanded)  
Modality: Face-to-face or synchronous online

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Standards Alignment
────────────────────────────────────────
• Common Core State Standards – Mathematics  
  – CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.HSS.CP.A.1 (Understand probability as a measure between 0 and 1)  
  – CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.HSS.CP.A.2 (Use sample spaces to determine probabilities)  
  – CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.HSS.CP.B.6 (Find conditional probability & independence)  
• NGSS Science Practice 4 (Analyzing & interpreting data)  
• ISTE Standard 1.4a (Data literacy)

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Learning Objectives (SWBAT…)
────────────────────────────────────────
1) Define and distinguish theoretical probability, experimental probability, and odds.  
2) Construct and analyze sample spaces using lists, tables, tree diagrams, and area models.  
3) Calculate the probability of single events and compound events (independent & mutually exclusive) using fractions, decimals, and percents.  
4) Critique statements of probability in real-world contexts (games, weather, medical testing).  
5) Use digital simulation tools (e.g., GeoGebra, Desmos, spreadsheet) to model random experiments and compare experimental to theoretical results.

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Required Prior Knowledge
────────────────────────────────────────
• Fractions, decimals, percents conversion  
• Basic multiplication & addition  
• Reading two-way tables

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Materials & Technology
────────────────────────────────────────
• Teacher: slides or interactive whiteboard; document camera; projector  
• Students: chromebooks or calculators; coin, six-sided die, deck of cards (optional); printed graphic organizer (sample space templates)  
• Online: wheel-of-names spinner, GeoGebra probability simulator, Kahoot!/Quizizz for formative checks, Jamboard or Padlet for brainstorming

────────────────────────────────────────
5. Vocabulary
────────────────────────────────────────
Experiment, outcome, event, sample space, probability, theoretical, experimental, relative frequency, independent, mutually exclusive, complement, union, intersection, “and” vs “or,” tree diagram.

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Lesson Flow (Two-Day Plan)
────────────────────────────────────────

DAY 1 (55 min) — Foundations & Single Events
------------------------------------------------
00-05 min  • Hook  
 “Would you bet on it?” slide shows 5 statements (e.g., “A randomly chosen person was born in July”). Students stand if they would bet $1 on the statement being true. Brief discussion leads to idea of probability as a confidence measure.

05-10 min  • Learning Targets & Agenda 
 Display objectives; students write one personal goal on sticky note.

10-20 min  • Exploration: Penny-Flip Quick Lab  
 Pairs flip a coin 30 times, record heads/tails tally in Google Sheet that auto-graphs class relative frequency. Real-time display shows convergence to 0.50 and introduces experimental probability.

20-35 min  • Direct Instruction  
 Mini-lecture with interactive checks:  
 – Definitions (experiment, outcome, event, sample space).  
 – Theoretical probability formula  P(E)= (# favorable)/(# total).  
 – Fraction-decimal-percent forms.  
 Use color-coded examples: spinner, marbles in a bag, weather forecast.

35-45 min  • Guided Practice: Sample Space Stations  
 Students rotate through 3 stations:  
 1) Coin-die combo → 2×6 table  
 2) 2-child gender tree diagram  
 3) Area model for picking colored tiles  
 For each station they list sample space, compute 2 given event probabilities, and photograph work.

45-52 min  • Formative Assessment (Kahoot!)  
 8 rapid-fire questions; teacher views mastery dashboard.

52-55 min  • Exit Ticket  
 Prompt: “What is one thing you can now explain to a friend?” & “Write a remaining question.”

Homework: Watch 5-min Edpuzzle video on independent vs dependent events; answer embedded checks.

DAY 2 (55 min) — Compound Events & Simulations
-------------------------------------------------
00-05 min  • Warm-Up  
 Review Kahoot! stats; address top misconception (e.g., confusing complement with complete set).

05-15 min  • Interactive Notes  
 Union (“or”) vs intersection (“and”); mutually exclusive vs independent; use Venn diagrams.

15-35 min  • Activity: “Carnival Game Design”  
 Groups of 3 receive a game brief (ring toss, spinner, card draw). Tasks:  
 a) Identify sample space, mark winning outcomes.  
 b) Compute theoretical probability of winning.  
 c) Use GeoGebra simulator (1000 trials) to produce experimental probability & histogram.  
 d) Decide fair ticket price (expected value extension for honors).  
 Deliverable: one-page pitch poster or 1-min Flip video.

35-45 min  • Whole-Class Share & Critique  
 Gallery walk; peers leave sticky notes evaluating fairness.

45-50 min  • Mini-Lesson: Odds & Real-World Media Literacy  
 Teacher shows newspaper horse-race odds; convert between odds & probability.

50-53 min  • Summative Quiz (Google Forms – auto graded, 5 questions)  
 Includes single-event, compound independent, complement, odds.

53-55 min  • Reflection  
 Students add to digital portfolio: two screenshots (coin lab, simulator) with 3-sentence reflection on how experimental probability approaches theoretical as trials increase.

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Differentiation & Accommodations
────────────────────────────────────────
• Scaffolded graphic organizers; sentence starters.  
• Color-coding, icons for ELL.  
• Extension: expected value & conditional probability problems.  
• Support: allow use of manipulatives, reduced-number trials, extra time.  
• Closed captioning on videos; chunked instructions.

────────────────────────────────────────
8. Assessment Plan
────────────────────────────────────────
Formative: observation, station work, Kahoot!, warm-ups, exit tickets.  
Summative: Day 2 quiz (70%), carnival poster rubric (30%).  
Rubric criteria: accuracy, completeness of sample space, justification, creativity, visual clarity.

────────────────────────────────────────
9. Anticipated Misconceptions
────────────────────────────────────────
• Confusing experimental with theoretical (“law of small numbers”).  
• Believing past outcomes influence independent events (“gambler’s fallacy”).  
• Mixing up “or” and “and.”  
• Probabilities over 1 or negative; forgetting denominator.  
Strategy: Address explicitly with counter-examples and simulations.

────────────────────────────────────────
10. Safety & Management
────────────────────────────────────────
• Coins/dice sanitized or virtual if needed.  
• Clear time limits for stations; roles (recorder, reporter, tech manager).  
• Device expectations contract posted.

────────────────────────────────────────
11. Teacher Reflection (post-lesson)
────────────────────────────────────────
• Were objectives met? Use quiz analytics, poster quality, student reflections.  
• Which station needed revision?  
• Note pacing issues for next cycle.

────────────────────────────────────────
12. Optional Extensions
────────────────────────────────────────
• Sports analytics project: use MLB batting averages to predict hits.  
• Medical testing Bayes’ theorem (honors).  
• Cross-curricular: English—analyze probability language in news headlines.

End of Lesson Plan
